title: crit-hub engine card (card.yaml)
description: An engine's hand-written record: what it is, what it measured and the README's prose. tools/check_engines.py is authoritative; it also checks figures against evidence files and README.md against the rendered card.

title.description: The README's title: <Model> @ <encoding> · <GPU> · <engine name>, or the engine name when it runs several.

summary.description: One line on what the engine does.

origin.description: crit: exported from a sealed crit candidate; external: built with any other toolkit.

name.description: GitHub account or organization; also the engine folder's <owner>.

license.description: SPDX id of the engine source, e.g. Apache-2.0.

source.description: Where the engine's source is: crit-labs/crit-engines for crit engines, the contributor's repository otherwise.

path.description: The engine's folder in that repository.

backend.description: The device API the engine runs on; cuda when left out.

gpu_arch.description: Architectures it is built for: sm_120a (cuda), gfx1201 (hip), apple9 (metal), a device family (vulkan).

cuda.description: CUDA toolkit (backend cuda). Quote it in YAML: "13.1".

rocm.description: ROCm version (backend hip). Quote it in YAML: "6.4".

metal.description: Metal Shading Language version (backend metal), like "3.2".

runtime.description: What the engine links, e.g. crit Core 0.5.0.

build.description: How crit pull builds a crit engine's source; leave it out when the source runs as it is.

command.description: Literal arguments, run in the engine/ folder of the pinned source; a first argument python is the Python crit runs in.

downloads.description: What to fetch besides the pinned checkpoint, each pinned by revision or sha256.

kind.description: drafter: weights the engine loads beside the checkpoint, given to it as context.drafters; artifact: a prebuilt tar archive of what the build adds to engine/, unpacked instead of building where its toolchain matches.

toolchain.description: An artifact's: what it was built with and for. crit pull unpacks it instead of building on a machine that matches all of it.

gpu_arch.description: Architectures its device code is compiled for, as requirements.gpu_arch.

cuda.description: CUDA version it was compiled with: the driver must run this version or a newer one.

rocm.description: ROCm version it was compiled with (backend hip).

python.description: Python its extension modules are built for, like "3.12"; leave it out when it has none.

checkpoints.description: The Hugging Face checkpoint of every measured or supported model, keyed by model id (qwen3.8-27b@NVFP4). card.lock.json lists the measured ones' files.

supports.description: Further GPU and model pairs the engine runs, not measured yet.

derived_from.description: The crit-hub engine the run that built this one started from (crit run create --from-engine); written by tools/export_engine.py.

built.description: What the run that built the engine took, from its cost.json (crit run cost): wall hours, candidates, the agent's tokens, their API-equivalent price in USD and the agent; written by tools/export_engine.py.

readme.description: The README's prose, markdown in block scalars (|), rendered in this order.

gpu.description: The card in lowercase, e.g. rtx5090.

figure.description: A positive number, or [low, high] across runs.

track.description: closed: crit Eval in either quality mode at that mode's protocol budget, one configuration for every workload loaded once, and the checkpoint's own draft layers as the only drafter where it has them; its result files' track.closed must qualify where they record it, and files from before those checks were judged in preserve at preserve's budget. open: anything else the protocol allows, a budget of its own, other drafters, settings per case.

by.description: Who measured it, when not the contributor: their GitHub account (tools/add_result.py, crit hub report).

measured_with.description: A crit Eval protocol (crit-eval-v0.2.0, crit-eval-v7) or how else it was measured (LocalMaxxing, your own benchmark).

measured_on.description: The day it was measured, YYYY-MM-DD (quoted); null when unknown, never for crit Eval.

quality_mode.description: The quality mode it was judged in, one of schemas/quality-modes.yaml (preserve, as_quantized, ...). crit Eval: what the result file's requirements.quality_mode records; otherwise your own statement. Every result states it.

hardware.description: One line naming the machine it ran on. crit Eval: what the result file's host records (left out when it records none); otherwise your own statement.

sampling.description: crit-eval-v7, only when the sampled decode was not measured at the model's generation_config.json: the result file's sampled_speed sampling_source and sampling.

stats.description: The six headline stats, in this order; null when not measured.

ttft_ms.description: Time to first token in ms.

vs_reference.description: Perplexity ratio against the reference, e.g. 1.001.

absolute.description: Absolute perplexity, when no reference was measured.

kld_mean.description: Mean KL divergence against the reference.

context_tokens.description: The maximum context it was measured at.

more.description: Further figures, shown after the stats.

greedy_decode_tok_s.description: crit-eval-v7: the greedy suite's decode; stats.decode_tok_s is the sampled decode.

throughput.description: Throughput with several requests at once, concurrency ascending: per concurrency, the requests' completion tokens per second together. crit Eval: its concurrency part's levels that qualified (concurrency.levels.<N>.aggregate_tps); otherwise the contributor's own report, shown as self-reported.

tok_s.description: Their completion tokens per second together; [low, high] across runs.

reproductions.description: The same GPU and model measured again with crit Eval on someone else's machine (tools/add_result.py, crit hub report), each from its own result files, which its figures must be.

by.description: Who measured it: their GitHub account.

measured_with.description: The crit Eval protocol its result files ran under.

evidence.description: evidence/crit-eval.json (and -2, -3 ...) for a crit Eval result; optionally evidence/self-reported.json otherwise.
